stories.headline: A contaminated plate, a holiday, and the first antibiotic
stories.summary: On 3 September 1928, Alexander Fleming returned to his laboratory from a holiday with his family in Suffolk and noticed that one of the culture plates he had left on a bench was contaminated with a fungus, and that the staphylococci around it had been destroyed. He shared the 1945 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Howard Florey and Ernst Chain for the discovery of penicillin.

stories.headline: The deepest point in the ocean, measured to the metre
stories.summary: The Challenger Deep is the deepest known point of the seabed, lying in the western Pacific at the southern end of the Mariana Trench. A 2021 study put its depth at 10,935 metres, give or take about six metres. The first descent by any vehicle was made by the United States Navy's bathyscaphe Trieste in January 1960.

stories.headline: The valley where the pharaohs were laid to rest
stories.summary: The Valley of the Kings is a wadi on the west bank of the Nile, opposite Thebes, the modern-day Luxor. For nearly 500 years rock-cut tombs were excavated there for the pharaohs and powerful nobles of Egypt's New Kingdom, and it is now known to contain 65 tombs and chambers. Howard Carter discovered the tomb of Tutankhamun there on 4 November 1922.
